questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Calcium channel blockers are used in:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Dihydropyridines such as amlodipine and nifedipine cause arteriolar vasodilatation and are first-line antihypertensives.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Non-dihydropyridines are negatively inotropic and worsen HFrEF; CCBs give no mortality benefit, so they are not a heart-failure treatment.

options.label: C
options.explanation: They reduce afterload and myocardial O2 demand and relieve coronary spasm, so they are used in stable and vasospastic angina.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Verapamil and diltiazem (class IV) slow AV nodal conduction, controlling SVT and AF rate.

questions.pearl: Verapamil plus a beta-blocker risks complete heart block and asystole; avoid IV verapamil in a beta-blocked patient.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Giant-cell pneumonia or secondary bacterial bronchopneumonia is the commonest cause of measles death.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Orchitis is a classic complication of mumps, not measles.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Measles involves the CNS as encephalitis (acute, post-infectious or inclusion-body), not as meningitis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: SSPE is a late (7-10 years) persistent measles virus infection of the brain with myoclonus and progressive dementia.

questions.pearl: Vitamin A in measles reduces mortality and corneal complications; give on two consecutive days.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: True allergy is rare but occurs, mainly with ester agents (PABA metabolite) or preservatives.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Systemic toxicity first blocks inhibitory cortical neurons, giving perioral numbness, tinnitus, twitching and then convulsions.

options.label: C
options.explanation: High systemic levels or high spinal spread cause respiratory depression or paralysis of respiratory muscles.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Sodium-channel blockade in the heart causes bradycardia, VT/VF and arrest; bupivacaine is the most cardiotoxic.

questions.pearl: Treat local anaesthetic systemic toxicity with 20% lipid emulsion (1.5 ml/kg bolus) alongside ALS.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Proteinuria >3.5 g/day (>40 mg/m2/h in children) is the defining feature.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Classic nephrotic syndrome (e.g. minimal change) is normotensive; hypertension points to a nephritic picture.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Macroscopic haematuria is a nephritic feature; nephrotic urine is frothy rather than red.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hypoalbuminaemia stimulates hepatic lipoprotein synthesis, causing hyperlipidaemia.

questions.pearl: Nephrotic tetrad: proteinuria >3.5 g/day, hypoalbuminaemia, oedema, hyperlipidaemia.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Restless, irritable child is a sign of some dehydration; lethargy or unconsciousness indicates severe.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Sunken eyes are present in both some and severe dehydration.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Not able to drink or drinking poorly is a severe dehydration sign; some dehydration drinks eagerly.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Slow skin pinch (<2 s) is some dehydration; very slowly (>2 s) is severe.

questions.pearl: IMCI: two of the listed signs are needed to classify some or severe dehydration; some dehydration gets Plan B ORS 75 ml/kg over 4 h.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Reduced potassium excretion makes hyperkalaemia a common CKD complication, so it is not the exception.

options.label: B
options.explanation: CKD causes anaemia from reduced erythropoietin; polycythaemia is not a complication (it is seen with renal tumours or post-transplant).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Uraemic pruritus from phosphate retention and secondary hyperparathyroidism is common in CKD.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Renal osteodystrophy results from phosphate retention, low calcitriol and secondary hyperparathyroidism.

questions.pearl: Anaemia of CKD is normocytic normochromic; correct iron first, then give erythropoietin aiming for Hb 10-12 g/dl.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: TBM gives a lymphocytic pleocytosis, usually 50-500 cells/mm3.

options.label: B
options.explanation: CSF glucose is low (often <50% of blood glucose) in TBM.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Protein is markedly raised in TBM, often 1-5 g/l, sometimes forming a cobweb clot.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Low CSF chloride is a classic, though nonspecific, finding in tuberculous meningitis.

questions.pearl: Cobweb coagulum on standing CSF suggests TBM; Froin syndrome (xanthochromia with very high protein) suggests spinal block.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: 0.9% NaCl contains 154 mmol/l sodium.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Normal saline has no potassium; Hartmann solution contains 5 mmol/l.

options.label: C
options.explanation: It contains 154 mmol/l chloride, more than plasma, so large volumes cause hyperchloraemic acidosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: No calcium; Ringer lactate contains about 2 mmol/l calcium.

questions.pearl: Normal saline: Na 154, Cl 154 mmol/l, osmolality about 308 mOsm/l.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Obstruction to LV outflow gives a slow-rising, low-volume (anacrotic) pulse.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Reduced stroke volume narrows the pulse pressure in severe AS.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A2 becomes soft or absent as the calcified valve stops moving; a loud S2 is not expected.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Tapping apex (palpable S1) is mitral stenosis; AS gives a heaving, pressure-loaded apex.

questions.pearl: Classic AS triad: angina, syncope, exertional dyspnoea; once symptomatic, valve replacement is indicated.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pneumonia affects the lung parenchyma, giving tachypnoea and crackles, not stridor.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Bronchial (lower airway) narrowing produces wheeze; stridor needs upper airway obstruction, as in laryngotracheobronchitis (croup).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Laryngeal inflammation narrows the upper airway, producing inspiratory stridor.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pulmonary TB causes cough and haemoptysis; stridor is not a usual feature.

questions.pearl: Croup (parainfluenza) gives barking cough with stridor; treat with oral dexamethasone and nebulised adrenaline if severe.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: BP of 160/110 mmHg or more defines severe pre-eclampsia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Epigastric or right upper quadrant pain reflects liver capsule stretch and warns of HELLP or eclampsia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pulmonary oedema is a severe feature from capillary leak and raised afterload.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pedal oedema is common in normal pregnancy and is not a severity criterion.

questions.pearl: Magnesium sulphate is the drug of choice to prevent and treat eclamptic fits; monitor reflexes, respiration and urine output.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: The injectable Vi vaccine is a subunit polysaccharide; only oral Ty21a typhoid vaccine is live.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Sabin OPV contains live attenuated poliovirus; IPV (Salk) is killed.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The intranasal cold-adapted influenza vaccine is live attenuated; the injectable form is inactivated.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Standard hepatitis A vaccines are formalin-inactivated whole virus.

questions.pearl: Live vaccines (BCG, OPV, MMR, varicella, yellow fever, oral typhoid) are avoided in pregnancy and immunosuppression.

questions.subject: Gynecology
questions.stem: Genital ulcer is caused by, except:

options.label: A
options.explanation: H. ducreyi causes chancroid, a painful soft genital ulcer, so it is not the exception.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Serovars L1-L3 cause lymphogranuloma venereum with a transient painless ulcer, so it is not the exception.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Primary syphilis gives a painless indurated chancre.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Gonorrhoea causes purulent urethral or cervical discharge, not genital ulceration.

questions.pearl: Painful ulcer: herpes, chancroid. Painless ulcer: syphilis, LGV, donovanosis.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cocaine blocks noradrenaline reuptake, stimulating the dilator pupillae.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Amphetamines release noradrenaline, producing sympathomimetic mydriasis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Opioids cause pinpoint pupils via the Edinger-Westphal nucleus.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Acetylcholinesterase inhibition causes muscarinic miosis.

questions.pearl: Pinpoint pupils: opioids, organophosphates, pontine haemorrhage. Dilated: TCA, atropine/datura, sympathomimetics.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Arthralgia is a minor criterion; migratory polyarthritis is the major one.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Fever is a minor Jones criterion.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Chorea is a major criterion and may be the sole manifestation, appearing months after infection.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pancarditis is a major criterion and the main cause of long-term morbidity.

questions.pearl: Jones major (CASES): carditis, arthritis, subcutaneous nodules, erythema marginatum, Sydenham chorea.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Entamoeba histolytica invades the colonic mucosa, causing flask-shaped ulcers and dysentery.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Shigella invades colonic epithelium, causing bacillary dysentery with blood and mucus.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Cholera toxin raises cAMP causing profuse painless rice-water diarrhoea without blood.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Rectal bleeding is a red flag that excludes IBS until proven otherwise.

questions.pearl: Bloody diarrhoea in children: treat as Shigella with ciprofloxacin for 3 days per WHO/IMCI.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Metronidazole is an antiprotozoal/anti-anaerobe with no role in anaphylaxis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Albendazole is an anthelmintic and does nothing for anaphylaxis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Neither drug reverses mast-cell mediator release; IM adrenaline is the treatment.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Anaphylaxis is not infective; antibiotics do not help and may be the trigger.

questions.pearl: Anaphylaxis: IM adrenaline 1:1000, 0.5 mg in adults (0.01 mg/kg in children) into the anterolateral thigh, repeat after 5 min.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Neisseria are Gram-negative diplococci.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Staphylococci are Gram-positive cocci in clusters, catalase positive.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Streptococci are Gram-positive cocci in chains, catalase negative.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Haemophilus is a Gram-negative coccobacillus.

questions.pearl: Catalase separates staphylococci (positive) from streptococci (negative); coagulase identifies S. aureus.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Group A and B streptococci cause osteomyelitis, the latter especially in neonates.

options.label: B
options.explanation: S. aureus is the commonest cause at all ages.

options.label: C
options.explanation: H. influenzae was important in young children before Hib vaccination.

options.label: D
options.explanation: E. coli and Salmonella occur in neonates, the elderly and sickle-cell disease.

questions.pearl: Salmonella osteomyelitis is classic in sickle-cell disease, though S. aureus is still common.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: SARS-CoV-2 is a positive-sense single-stranded RNA coronavirus.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Transmission is by respiratory droplets, aerosols and contact.

options.label: C
options.text: First known case identified in Wuhan
options.explanation: The first cluster was reported in Wuhan, China, in December 2019.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Severe disease causes viral pneumonia and ARDS needing oxygen or ventilation.

questions.pearl: SARS-CoV-2 enters cells via the ACE2 receptor using its spike protein.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Plasma leakage from increased capillary permeability causes ascites.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Pleural effusion, often right-sided, is a sign of plasma leakage.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A pulse pressure of 20 mmHg or less signals impending dengue shock.

options.label: D
options.text: Rise in haematocrit for age and sex
options.explanation: A rise of 20% or more in haematocrit marks haemoconcentration from leakage.

questions.pearl: Critical phase of dengue starts around defervescence (day 3-7); watch for warning signs, not the fever.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Raised sinusoidal pressure with hypoalbuminaemia and sodium retention causes ascites.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Palmar erythema reflects hyperoestrogenism of hepatocellular failure, not portal hypertension.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Congestive splenomegaly with hypersplenism is a cardinal sign.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Portosystemic collaterals at the oesophagogastric junction rupture when HVPG exceeds 12 mmHg.

questions.pearl: HVPG >5 mmHg defines portal hypertension; >10 is clinically significant; >12 mmHg risks variceal bleeding.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Obesity is associated with hypertension, not hypotension.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Type 1 DM is autoimmune; obesity predisposes to type 2 via insulin resistance.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Fat deposition around the pharynx causes upper airway collapse during sleep.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Excess load accelerates osteoarthritis of the knees and hips.

questions.pearl: Asian BMI cut-offs: overweight 23 or more, obese 27.5 or more (WHO Asia-Pacific uses 25).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Reduced thyroid hormone lowers sinus node rate.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Retained bile salts have a vagotonic effect on the SA node causing bradycardia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Catecholamine excess causes tachycardia and palpitations.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Acute exercise raises heart rate; only trained athletes have resting bradycardia.

questions.pearl: Cushing reflex: hypertension, bradycardia and irregular breathing indicate raised intracranial pressure.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Carbamazepine is an anticonvulsant mood stabiliser used in bipolar disorder.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Lithium is the prototype mood stabiliser, reducing manic and depressive relapse and suicide.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Valproate is a first-line mood stabiliser for acute mania and maintenance.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Haloperidol is a typical antipsychotic used to control acute agitation, not as a mood stabiliser.

questions.pearl: Lithium therapeutic range 0.6-1.0 mmol/l; toxicity causes coarse tremor, ataxia and confusion.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Ectopic endometrium bleeds cyclically, causing progressive secondary dysmenorrhoea.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Endometrium within myometrium causes dysmenorrhoea and menorrhagia with a bulky uterus.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Ovarian tumours are usually silent or cause pressure symptoms, not cyclical menstrual pain.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cervical polyps cause intermenstrual or postcoital bleeding, not dysmenorrhoea.

questions.pearl: Primary dysmenorrhoea is prostaglandin-mediated; NSAIDs are first-line.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Creatinine assesses renal function.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Albumin reflects hepatic synthetic function over weeks (half-life about 20 days).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Bilirubin reflects hepatic uptake, conjugation and excretion.

options.label: D
options.explanation: CRP is an acute-phase marker of inflammation, not a test of liver function.

questions.pearl: Prothrombin time is the best acute marker of hepatic synthetic function because factor VII has a 6-hour half-life.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Glomerular basement membrane thickening and mesangial expansion (Kimmelstiel-Wilson) are microvascular.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Stroke is a macrovascular complication from atherosclerosis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hypertensive retinopathy is due to hypertension; the diabetic microvascular eye lesion is diabetic retinopathy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: MI is macrovascular (coronary atherosclerosis).

questions.pearl: Microvascular: retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy. Macrovascular: coronary, cerebrovascular, peripheral arterial disease.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Present at birth and disappears by 4-6 months; persistence suggests neurological damage.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A primitive feeding reflex present at birth, waning by about 4 months.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Head turns toward a cheek stimulus; disappears by about 4 months.

options.label: D
options.explanation: An extensor plantar response is normal in infancy until about 1-2 years; later it indicates UMN lesion.

questions.pearl: Primitive reflexes reappearing in adults (grasp, snout, palmomental) are frontal release signs.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Warfarin, heparin and antiplatelets are common systemic causes, especially in the elderly.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Digital trauma to Little area is the commonest cause in children.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hypertension, not hypotension, is associated with epistaxis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma causes profuse recurrent epistaxis in adolescent males.

questions.pearl: Little area (Kiesselbach plexus) on the anterior septum is the site of 90% of nosebleeds.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Inability to complete sentences in one breath is a criterion of acute severe asthma.

options.label: B
options.explanation: RR of 25/min or more in adults defines acute severe asthma (BTS).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Chronic cough is a feature of poorly controlled asthma, not a severity criterion of an acute attack.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Acute severe asthma gives tachycardia (110/min or more); bradycardia signals a life-threatening attack.

questions.pearl: Life-threatening asthma: PEF <33%, SpO2 <92%, silent chest, cyanosis, bradycardia, exhaustion, normal or rising PaCO2.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: The brain lies in the cranial cavity, separated from the orbit by the orbital plate of the frontal bone.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The six extraocular muscles and levator palpebrae lie within the orbit.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Olfactory nerves pass through the cribriform plate into the nasal cavity, not the orbit.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The globe occupies the anterior part of the orbit.

questions.pearl: Orbital contents include CN II, III, IV, VI, branches of V1, ciliary ganglion, ophthalmic vessels and orbital fat.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Lid closure and blinking shield the cornea from glare and injury.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Blinking spreads the tear film and meibomian lipid, preventing corneal drying.

options.label: C
options.text: Eye opens when orbicularis oculi contracts
options.explanation: Orbicularis oculi (facial nerve) closes the eye; levator palpebrae superioris (oculomotor) opens it.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Lids are a mechanical barrier; antimicrobial action comes from lysozyme and IgA in tears.

questions.pearl: Facial nerve palsy causes lagophthalmos and exposure keratopathy; third nerve palsy causes ptosis.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: ATP7B mutation on chromosome 13, inherited autosomal recessively.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Haemophilia A and B are X-linked recessive.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Most cases are autosomal dominant (ankyrin, spectrin defects).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Beta- and alpha-thalassaemia are autosomal recessive globin chain disorders.

questions.pearl: Enzyme deficiencies are usually AR; structural protein defects are usually AD.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.stem: Excessive vomiting in early pregnancy is associated with:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Eclampsia occurs after 20 weeks, not in early pregnancy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Pre-eclampsia appears after 20 weeks and is not a cause of early pregnancy vomiting.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Higher hCG levels in multiple pregnancy increase nausea and vomiting.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hyperemesis is intractable vomiting with dehydration, ketosis and weight loss over 5%.

questions.pearl: High hCG states (twins, molar pregnancy) predispose to hyperemesis; exclude a mole with ultrasound.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Reduced peripheral resistance from progesterone lowers BP, maximal in the mid-trimester.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cardiac output rises by 40-50%, peaking by 30-34 weeks.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Placental hCG, oestrogen, progesterone and hPL drive most maternal adaptations.

options.label: D
options.text: Increase in GFR leading to albuminuria
options.explanation: GFR rises by 50%, causing physiological glycosuria; significant proteinuria (>300 mg/day) is pathological.

questions.pearl: Physiological anaemia of pregnancy: plasma volume rises about 50% versus red cell mass about 20-30%.

questions.subject: Gynecology
questions.stem: Itching vaginal discharge is caused by:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Chlamydia is often asymptomatic or causes mucopurulent cervicitis without itching.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Frothy greenish-yellow discharge with pruritus and strawberry cervix.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Curdy white discharge with intense vulval itching.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Psoriasis may affect the vulval skin but does not cause vaginal discharge.

questions.pearl: Bacterial vaginosis: fishy thin grey discharge, clue cells, pH >4.5, usually not itchy.

questions.subject: Gynecology
questions.stem: A 36-year-old primigravida presents with amenorrhoea, sudden severe lower abdominal pain, syncope and slight vaginal bleeding. The commonest site of ectopic pregnancy is:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Intraligamentary pregnancy is rare, usually secondary to tubal rupture.

options.label: B
options.explanation: About 70-80% of ectopic pregnancies are ampullary.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Isthmic ectopics (about 12%) rupture early but are less common.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Abdominal pregnancy is rare (about 1%).

questions.pearl: Interstitial ectopic ruptures latest and bleeds most; isthmic ruptures earliest.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.stem: A woman at 37 weeks with APH and severe abdominal pain most likely has:

options.label: A
options.explanation: At 37 weeks the pregnancy is term, and labour pains are intermittent rather than severe and continuous.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Placenta praevia causes painless, causeless, recurrent bleeding.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Retroplacental haemorrhage causes painful bleeding with a tense, tender uterus.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A vaginal tear bleeds locally without severe abdominal pain.

questions.pearl: Abruption: shock out of proportion to visible bleeding; watch for DIC and Couvelaire uterus.

questions.subject: Gynecology
questions.stem: Carcinoma cervix can be prevented by:

options.label: A
options.explanation: IUCDs do not prevent HPV infection and are not a cervical cancer prevention strategy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Long-term combined pill use slightly increases cervical cancer risk.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Vaccines against HPV 16 and 18 prevent about 70% of cervical cancers.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Genital hygiene and safe sexual practices reduce HPV and STI exposure.

questions.pearl: WHO 90-70-90 target: 90% HPV vaccinated by 15, 70% screened, 90% treated.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: p53, the guardian of the genome, arrests the cell cycle or triggers apoptosis after DNA damage.

options.label: B
options.explanation: RB holds cells in G1 by binding E2F; loss causes retinoblastoma and osteosarcoma.

options.label: C
options.explanation: RET is a proto-oncogene; gain-of-function mutation causes MEN 2 and medullary thyroid carcinoma.

options.label: D
options.explanation: APC loss causes familial adenomatous polyposis and starts the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma sequence.

questions.pearl: Tumour suppressor genes need two hits (Knudson); oncogenes need one activating mutation.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: H2S is a toxic gas but not a recognised greenhouse gas.

options.label: B
options.explanation: CO2 is the main anthropogenic greenhouse gas.

options.label: C
options.explanation: N2O is a potent long-lived greenhouse gas from fertilisers and combustion.

options.label: D
options.explanation: CFCs are powerful greenhouse gases and also deplete stratospheric ozone.

questions.pearl: Main greenhouse gases: CO2, methane, nitrous oxide, CFCs and water vapour.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Muscarinic stimulation causes bronchospasm and bronchorrhoea.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Pinpoint pupils from muscarinic action on the sphincter pupillae.

options.label: C
options.explanation: OP poisoning causes urinary incontinence; retention is an anticholinergic (atropine) effect.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Excess sweating occurs; dry skin points to anticholinergic toxicity.

questions.pearl: Muscarinic DUMBELS: diarrhoea, urination, miosis, bronchorrhoea, emesis, lacrimation, salivation.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.text: A baby smiles socially by 3 months
options.explanation: Social smile appears at 6-8 weeks and is well established by 3 months.

options.label: B
options.text: Neck control is achieved by 5 months
options.explanation: Head control is complete by about 4 months, so a 5-month-old should have it.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Independent sitting is achieved by 6-8 months.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Crawling typically starts around 9-10 months.

questions.pearl: Gross motor: head control 3-4 months, sits 6-8, stands with support 9, walks alone 12-15 months.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Anterior duodenal ulcers perforate, causing peritonitis and free gas under the diaphragm.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Healing with fibrosis causes gastric outlet obstruction with hypochloraemic alkalosis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Posterior ulcers erode the gastroduodenal artery causing major haemorrhage.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hourglass deformity results from scarring of a lesser-curve gastric ulcer, not a duodenal ulcer.

questions.pearl: Anterior DU perforates; posterior DU bleeds (gastroduodenal artery).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Thalassaemia causes anaemia; thrombocytopenia occurs only with hypersplenism.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Marrow suppression and immune destruction cause thrombocytopenia in dengue.

options.label: C
options.explanation: HSP is a small-vessel IgA vasculitis with normal platelet count.

options.label: D
options.explanation: HELLP is haemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelets.

questions.pearl: Palpable purpura with normal platelets suggests vasculitis such as HSP.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Widespread P. falciparum resistance makes chloroquine unsuitable for severe malaria.

options.label: B
options.explanation: IV quinine is an effective alternative when artesunate is unavailable.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Artemisinin derivatives are the drugs of choice for severe falciparum malaria.

options.label: D
options.explanation: IV artesunate is first-line, reducing mortality compared with quinine.

questions.pearl: Quinine causes hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia; check glucose regularly.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cephalosporins are beta-lactams inhibiting cell wall synthesis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Aminoglycosides bind the 30S subunit causing misreading of mRNA.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Neomycin is an aminoglycoside acting on the 30S subunit.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Tetracyclines block aminoacyl-tRNA binding to the 30S subunit.

questions.pearl: 30S inhibitors: aminoglycosides, tetracyclines. 50S: chloramphenicol, macrolides, clindamycin, linezolid.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Viral hepatitis that causes chronic infection:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Faeco-oral HAV is self-limiting and never chronic.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Becomes chronic in 90% of neonates and about 5% of adults.

options.label: C
options.explanation: About 70-80% of HCV infections become chronic.

options.label: D
options.explanation: HEV is usually acute and self-limiting; chronicity occurs only in immunosuppressed patients.

questions.pearl: HEV in pregnancy carries up to 20% mortality from fulminant hepatic failure.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Abundant in breast milk compared with cow milk:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Human milk is whey-dominant (whey:casein about 60:40); casein is much lower than in cow milk.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Breast milk protein is low (about 1.1 g/dl versus 3.3 g/dl in cow milk), suiting the immature kidney.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Breast milk is richer in vitamin C than cow milk, which is further lost on boiling.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Iron content is low in both, though breast milk iron is better absorbed (about 50%).

questions.pearl: Breast milk is richer in lactose, whey, PUFA, vitamins A and C and lactoferrin than cow milk.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Chronic suppurative lung disease is a classic cause of clubbing.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Acute pneumonia does not cause clubbing.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Chronic suppuration in lung abscess causes clubbing.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Simple coal-worker and silicotic pneumoconiosis do not cause clubbing; asbestosis is the exception.

questions.pearl: COPD does not cause clubbing; if present, look for bronchial carcinoma.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Raised hydrostatic pressure gives a transudate.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Low oncotic pressure gives a transudate.

options.label: C
options.explanation: TB causes a lymphocytic exudate with high ADA.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Infarction causes an exudative, often blood-stained effusion.

questions.pearl: Light criteria: exudate if pleural/serum protein >0.5, LDH ratio >0.6, or pleural LDH >2/3 upper limit of normal.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: The face has the highest density of sebaceous glands, hence acne.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Palms lack sebaceous glands and hair follicles.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Abdominal skin has hair follicles with sebaceous glands.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Soles lack sebaceous glands but have abundant eccrine sweat glands.

questions.pearl: Free sebaceous glands (not attached to hair) include meibomian glands, Fordyce spots and Montgomery tubercles.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Tenderness at the junction of the lateral and middle thirds of the spinoumbilical line is classic.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Murphy sign indicates acute cholecystitis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Low-grade fever is typical; high fever suggests perforation.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Nausea and vomiting usually follow the onset of pain.

questions.pearl: Murphy triad of appendicitis: pain, vomiting, fever in that order; Alvarado score aids diagnosis.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Upper motor neuron lesion is associated with:

options.label: A
options.explanation: UMN lesions cause spastic paralysis; flaccidity is LMN (except in acute spinal shock).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Deep tendon reflexes are exaggerated in UMN lesions.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Extensor plantar response is the hallmark of UMN lesion.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Significant wasting is LMN; UMN lesions show only mild disuse atrophy.

questions.pearl: UMN: spasticity, hyperreflexia, clonus, extensor plantar. LMN: flaccidity, areflexia, wasting, fasciculation.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Posterior displacement of the distal fragment gives an S-shaped deformity with intact three-point relationship.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Pain and swelling restrict elbow movement.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Marked swelling around the elbow develops quickly.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Severe pain follows a fall on the outstretched hand.

questions.pearl: Watch for brachial artery injury and Volkmann ischaemic contracture; malunion leads to cubitus varus.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery
questions.stem: Recognised causes of non-union of a fracture:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Impacted fragments have good contact and stability, so they unite readily.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Open fractures carry infection, periosteal stripping and soft-tissue loss, all leading to non-union.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Ankylosis is joint fusion, not a cause of fracture non-union.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A gap between fragments from distraction prevents bridging callus.

questions.pearl: Non-union is common in scaphoid, neck of femur and lower third tibia due to poor blood supply.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery
questions.stem: Unilateral undescended testis is associated with:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Fertility is largely preserved in unilateral cryptorchidism; infertility is mainly a risk in bilateral cases.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Risk of testicular germ-cell tumour, especially seminoma, is raised several-fold.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Abnormal attachment and mobility predispose an undescended testis to torsion.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Combination with hypospadias raises concern for a DSD and is uncommon in isolated unilateral UDT.

questions.pearl: Orchidopexy is recommended at 6-12 months to preserve spermatogenesis and allow examination for tumour.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Club foot is congenital talipes equinovarus.

options.label: B
options.explanation: CTEV is present at birth, idiopathic in most cases.

options.label: C
options.text: Most commonly of the equinovalgus variety
options.explanation: The common type is equinovarus (plantarflexed, inverted, adducted forefoot).

options.label: D
options.explanation: It is associated with oligohydramnios, breech and neuromuscular disease, not placenta praevia.

questions.pearl: CTEV is treated by Ponseti serial casting, correcting cavus first, then adductus, varus and equinus (CAVE).

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Stress ulceration of the stomach or duodenum occurs after major burns.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Burns cause hypovolaemic shock from plasma loss; neurogenic shock follows spinal cord injury.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The hypermetabolic stress response causes hyperglycaemia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cushing ulcer follows head injury or raised intracranial pressure.

questions.pearl: Parkland formula: 4 ml x kg x %TBSA of Hartmann solution in 24 h, half in the first 8 h from the time of burn.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: A first-generation cephalosporin with no anti-pseudomonal activity.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A third-generation cephalosporin with strong anti-pseudomonal activity.

options.label: C
options.explanation: An antipseudomonal ureidopenicillin, usually given with tazobactam.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A second-generation cephalosporin without anti-pseudomonal activity.

questions.pearl: Anti-pseudomonal agents: piperacillin-tazobactam, ceftazidime, cefepime, carbapenems (not ertapenem), aztreonam, aminoglycosides, ciprofloxacin.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Brown-Sequard syndrome is characterised by loss of:

options.label: A
options.text: Voluntary movement on the same side
options.explanation: Corticospinal tracts have already crossed, so weakness is ipsilateral.

options.label: B
options.text: Pain sensation on the opposite side
options.explanation: Spinothalamic fibres cross within 1-2 segments, so pain loss is contralateral.

options.label: C
options.text: Thermal sensation on the same side
options.explanation: Temperature travels with pain in the spinothalamic tract and is lost contralaterally.

options.label: D
options.text: Fine touch on the same side
options.explanation: Dorsal columns ascend uncrossed, so fine touch, vibration and proprioception are lost ipsilaterally.

questions.pearl: Hemisection: ipsilateral motor and dorsal column loss, contralateral pain and temperature loss.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cortisol increases hepatic gluconeogenesis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: They reduce glucose uptake in muscle and fat, causing insulin resistance.

options.label: C
options.explanation: They mobilise fatty acids, while redistributing fat centrally.

options.label: D
options.explanation: They are catabolic, causing proximal myopathy and thin skin.

questions.pearl: Cortisol is diabetogenic: hyperglycaemia, central obesity, muscle wasting are classic Cushing features.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Heparin is a large charged molecule not absorbed orally or sublingually; it is given IV or SC.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Sulphate and carboxyl groups make it the strongest organic acid in the body.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Protamine sulphate reverses heparin; vitamin K reverses warfarin.

options.label: D
options.text: Unfractionated heparin is better than LMWH
options.explanation: LMWH has predictable kinetics, SC dosing, no routine monitoring and less HIT.

questions.pearl: Monitor UFH with aPTT; LMWH with anti-Xa if needed (renal failure, pregnancy, obesity).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Amino acids such as lysine and arginine form soluble calcium complexes, enhancing absorption.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Oxalates form insoluble calcium oxalate, reducing absorption.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Calcitriol induces calbindin and TRPV6 in enterocytes, increasing absorption.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Iron overload does not enhance calcium absorption.

questions.pearl: Phytates (cereals) and oxalates (spinach) reduce calcium absorption; acidity and lactose enhance it.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Bile acids, conjugated with glycine or taurine as bile salts, are the main organic solute of bile.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Bile contains negligible protein; it is not a recognised constituent.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Cholesterol is secreted in bile, kept in solution by bile salts and lecithin.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Bile aids absorption of vitamins A, D, E, K but does not contain them as constituents.

questions.pearl: Cholesterol stones form when the bile salt/lecithin to cholesterol ratio falls (lithogenic bile).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Oral lichen planus can leave post-inflammatory mucosal pigmentation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Malar rash of SLE is facial skin erythema sparing nasolabial folds, not mucosal pigmentation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Listed in the source as a cause of mucosal pigmentation; oral involvement is uncommon but reported.

options.label: D
options.explanation: High ACTH stimulates melanocytes, pigmenting buccal mucosa, palmar creases and scars.

questions.pearl: Peutz-Jeghers: perioral and buccal mucosal pigmentation with hamartomatous GI polyps.
